name: Mehetabel
title: Edomite Queen
summary: Mehetabel was the wife of Hadar (also called Hadad), the last king of Edom mentioned in the genealogies in Genesis and 1 Chronicles. She was the daughter of Matred, who was the daughter of Me-Zahab. She is primarily known through the lists of Edomite kings that describe the rulers of Edom before Israel had kings.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as Hadar's wife in Genesis
keyEvents.description: Mehetabel is mentioned as the wife of Hadar, the last king of Edom, in the genealogy of Esau's descendants. She is identified as the daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Me-Zahab.

keyEvents.title: The List of Edomite Kings in Genesis
keyEvents.description: Mehetabel appears in the context of the list of Edomite kings who reigned before any Israelite king ruled, highlighting Edom's early political organization.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Genealogy of Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Mehetabel is mentioned again as Hadar's wife in the parallel list of kings in 1 Chronicles, which presents the rulers of Edom as part of the broader family history.

keyEvents.title: The Lineages of Edom in 1 Chronicles
keyEvents.description: The broader context of 1 Chronicles places Mehetabel within the descendants of Esau and the Edomite tribes that were neighbors and relatives to Israel.
